content:
**#710 is 1-of-3 alive after #709, and the survivor is literally #723**

**What**: #710 was written against PR #703's head. #703 was closed WITHOUT merging and #709 replaced the approach, so #710's findings had to be re-measured rather than assumed. Measured against `main` @ `29760a9`:

**Finding 1 — an unterminated FOREIGN fence swallows a real declaration: STILL LIVE.**
```
parseGraphBlock('```console\n$ gh pr checks\n\n```brain-graph/1\ntrack: A\nblocks: [7]\n```')  =>  null
```
This is **the same defect as #723**, whose fourth shape is exactly this input. Not a related issue — the same line of missing code (`epic-graph.mjs` never destructures `skipped`).

**Finding 2 — near-miss tags (`yml`, `YAML`, `yaml title="x"`): FIXED, and upgraded.** They no longer answer `null`. They now return a loud `{ok:false, error}` naming the migration: *"the declaration is the fence tag since #709, not a `protocol:` scalar — retag the block at body line 1 as ```brain-graph/1`."* #709's tag selector dissolved the whole class — the yaml-alias question stopped existing when `yaml` stopped being the selector.

**Finding 3 — legal CommonMark closers accused of never closing: FIXED by #722.** Both an indented closer and a longer-run closer now parse and return the graph, instead of the fabricated *"never closed"* accusation.

**Consequence for sequencing**: #723 and #710 are one piece of work, not two. Wiring `skipped` into `epic-graph.mjs` kills #723 and #710's only surviving finding at once; #710 then closes with findings 2 and 3 recorded as fixed-by-#709/#722, each with its measurement.

**Method note**: this is the third time this session that re-measuring a written claim changed the answer. A ticket filed against a PR head is a claim about a tree that may no longer exist — #703 never merged, so two thirds of #710 was already dead and nothing said so.

**Related**: [[discovery/issue-723-skipped-never-wired]].
